## Purpose

This procedure describes the workflow for exporting raw data from the
Bio-Rad QX200 ddPCR system, performing quality control checks,
calculating gene copy numbers normalized to soil mass or DNA
concentration, and conducting statistical analyses of nitrogen cycle
gene abundance data. The SOP links the instrument output from
[SOP-L701](SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd) to reproducible
analysis scripts written in R [@rcoreteam2024].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Interpretation and analysis of QX200 ddPCR data
  (QuantaSoft or QuantaSoft Analysis Pro output) for nitrogen-cycle
  functional genes (*amoA*, *nirK*, *nirS*, *nosZ*, *nifH*, *nrfA*)
  from environmental soil samples, quantified in absolute units
  (copies per gram dry soil or copies per nanogram DNA)
- **Does not apply to:** Operating the instrument (see SOP-L214);
  assay or primer design and validation (see
  [SOP-L701](SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd)); amplicon
  sequencing, metagenomics, or qPCR data from other platforms
- **Location:** Instrument computer (QuantaSoft) for export and
  threshold review; RStudio Server for analysis (see
  [SOP-L801 RStudio and GitHub](SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd))


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                |
|:------------------|:----------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve analysis pipeline and interpretation  |
| Trained Personnel | Export data, run QC, perform analysis         |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent analysis |


## Definitions

- **Amplitude threshold:** The fluorescence intensity boundary set in
  QuantaSoft (or QuantaSoft Analysis Pro) that separates positive
  droplets (containing amplified target) from negative droplets;
  correct threshold placement is the single most critical step in
  ddPCR data analysis and must be reviewed manually for each plate
  [@biorad_qx200_2024].
- **Copies per microliter (copies/µL):** The absolute concentration
  of target DNA in the final ddPCR reaction volume as calculated by
  Poisson statistics from the fraction of positive droplets; must be
  back-calculated through all dilution steps to report concentration
  in the original sample [@hindson2011].
- **Droplet count filter:** A minimum threshold of accepted droplets
  per well (10,000 recommended) below which the Poisson estimate is
  unreliable; wells below this threshold must be excluded from analysis
  [@biorad_qx200_2024].
- **DMINQ (Digital Minimum Information for Publication of Quantitative
  Digital PCR Experiments):** The community standard for reporting ddPCR
  data [@dmiqe2020]; specifies required metadata including droplet
  count, threshold method, NTC results, and normalization approach.
- **NTC (no-template control):** A reaction well containing all
  reagents except DNA template; run on every plate to detect reagent
  or consumable contamination; must show 0 or fewer than 3 positive
  droplets per well [@biorad_appsguide2018].
- **Normalization:** The process of expressing gene copy numbers
  relative to a common denominator (total DNA concentration in ng/µL,
  or dry soil mass in g) to allow comparison across samples and studies;
  both normalizations should be reported when possible.
- **Poisson correction:** The statistical calculation applied by
  QuantaSoft to convert the fraction of positive droplets to an
  absolute copy number per microliter, correcting for the probability
  that a single droplet may contain more than one target molecule
  [@hindson2011].
- **QLp file:** The proprietary binary data file format produced by
  the Bio-Rad QX200 system; contains raw droplet amplitude data,
  QuantaSoft threshold settings, and computed results; must be archived
  unmodified before any downstream analysis.
- **Rain:** Droplets with intermediate fluorescence amplitude falling
  between the positive and negative clusters in the amplitude plot;
  indicates suboptimal amplification, partial inhibition, or primer
  issues; quantified as the percentage of events in the intermediate
  cluster and should be documented [@lievens2016; @biorad_appsguide2018].


## Why ddPCR for This Application

Quantitative PCR (qPCR) infers target abundance from amplification
kinetics against a standard curve, so its accuracy depends on
amplification efficiency and on curve quality. ddPCR instead partitions
each reaction into roughly 20,000 nanoliter droplets, amplifies to
endpoint within each droplet, and counts droplets as positive or
negative. The fraction of positive droplets is fit to a Poisson
distribution to recover the starting concentration in copies per
microliter, with no standard curve required [@hindson2011;
@biorad_appsguide2018].

For soil nitrogen-cycle work, this matters for several reasons:

- **Absolute, comparable counts.** Copy numbers are returned directly
  in copies per microliter, which can be normalized to soil mass or
  DNA and compared across plates, runs, and studies without a shared
  standard curve.
- **Tolerance of inhibitors.** Soil DNA extracts carry humic acids and
  other PCR inhibitors. Endpoint partitioning is less sensitive to
  partial inhibition than the kinetic measurement that qPCR depends on,
  although inhibition should still be checked (§6) [@hindson2011].
- **Precision for small differences.** The large number of partitions
  lets ddPCR resolve modest fold-changes in gene abundance between
  treatments [@hindson2011].
- **Low-abundance targets.** Genes such as *nosZ* or *nifH* are often
  present at low copy numbers relative to bulk DNA; partitioning
  improves the signal-to-noise ratio for rare targets.

These properties are the reason functional-gene abundance is
increasingly reported in absolute units when relating microbial
communities to nitrogen cycling processes [@levybooth2014].


## The Soil Nitrogen Cycle and Functional Gene Markers

Soil nitrogen transformations are carried out by distinct microbial
guilds, each defined by the enzymes (and therefore the genes) it
carries. Quantifying these marker genes provides a direct,
culture-independent estimate of the genetic potential for each process
[@kuypers2018; @levybooth2014].

| Gene        | Process / guild                              | What the abundance indicates | Primary reference |
|:------------|:---------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------|:------------------|
| *amoA* (AOB) | Ammonia oxidation, bacterial | Bacterial ammonia-oxidizer potential; first, rate-limiting step of nitrification | @rotthauwe1997 |
| *amoA* (AOA) | Ammonia oxidation, archaeal | Archaeal ammonia-oxidizer potential; often dominant in low-N, acidic soils | @francis2005 |
| *nirK*      | Nitrite reduction (denitrification) | Cu-type nitrite-reductase potential | @henry2006 |
| *nirS*      | Nitrite reduction (denitrification) | cd~1~-type nitrite-reductase potential | @braker2000 |
| *nosZ*      | Nitrous oxide reduction | N~2~O-reductase potential; capacity to reduce N~2~O to N~2~ | @henry2006 |
| *nifH*      | Nitrogen fixation | Diazotroph potential; biological N~2~ fixation | @levybooth2014 |
| *nrfA*      | DNRA | Retains N in system as NH~4~^+^ | @levybooth2014 |


## From Instrument Output to Quality-Controlled Data

### Reviewing and Exporting Data

Instrument operation and the QuantaSoft interface are covered in
SOP-L214. For analysis, the entry point is the exported well-level
data.

1. Open the completed experiment file (`.qlp`) in QuantaSoft and
   confirm the positive/negative threshold for each well. Re-apply
   thresholds manually in QuantaSoft Analysis Pro if needed, and
   record any change in the lab notebook.
2. Export with **Options > Export CSV** to produce a well-level results
   file. Key columns include `Well`, `Sample`, `Target`,
   `Concentration` (Poisson-corrected copies/µL [@hindson2011]),
   `Positives`, `Negatives`, `AcceptedDroplets`,
   `MeanAmplitudeOfPositives`, and `MeanAmplitudeOfNegatives`.
3. Name the file `YYYY-MM-DD_gene_project_plate.csv`.
4. Archive both the `.qlp` and the exported `.csv` to the lab shared
   drive under `ddPCR_raw_data/` before any analysis begins.

::: {.callout-warning}
#### Data Integrity

- Never overwrite raw exported data files. Work only with copies.
- Back up raw `.qlp` files immediately after each run.
- All analysis scripts must be version-controlled in the lab GitHub
  repository.
:::

### Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

Apply these checks before any analysis, following the data-quality
expectations set out for digital PCR reporting [@dmiqe2020;
@biorad_appsguide2018].

1. **Droplet count filter.** Exclude wells with fewer than 10,000
   accepted droplets; below this, the Poisson estimate is unreliable
   [@biorad_qx200_2024].
2. **No-template controls (NTC).** NTC wells must show 0 or fewer than
   3 positive droplets. More than 3 positives indicates contamination;
   rerun the affected target or plate.
3. **Extraction blanks.** Blanks carried from DNA extraction
   ([SOP-L700](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd)) must fall below the NTC
   threshold. Elevated counts point to contamination in the extraction
   workflow. Note that direct soil extraction is itself a known source
   of quantitative bias [@frostegard1999], so blanks and recovery
   checks matter for absolute numbers.
4. **Positive controls.** gBlock serial dilution positive controls
   must return concentrations within 20% of expected values across
   the linear range [@huggett2013].
5. **Rain.** Document the percentage of rain droplets per well. Assays
   with persistent high rain (> 10--15% of events) should be flagged
   and the primer or cycling conditions reviewed [@lievens2016].


## Calculating Gene Copy Numbers

### From Reaction to Sample

The concentration reported by QuantaSoft is in copies per microliter
of the final ddPCR reaction. To convert to copies per gram dry soil:

$$
N_{\text{soil}} =
C_{\text{rxn}} \times V_{\text{rxn}} \times D \times
\frac{V_{\text{elution}}}{V_{\text{rxn input}}} \times
\frac{1}{m_{\text{dry soil}}}
$$

where:

- $C_{\text{rxn}}$ = QuantaSoft-reported concentration (copies/µL)
- $V_{\text{rxn}}$ = total ddPCR reaction volume (typically 20 µL)
- $D$ = dilution factor applied to the extract before the reaction
- $V_{\text{elution}}$ = total DNA extract volume (µL)
- $V_{\text{rxn input}}$ = volume of extract added to the reaction (µL)
- $m_{\text{dry soil}}$ = mass of dry soil extracted (g)

### R Implementation

```{r}
#| label: copy-number-calculation
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# =============================================================================
# ddPCR copy number normalization (SOP-L702)
# =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)

# Import well-level QuantaSoft export
raw <- read_csv("2025-05-14_amoA_wetland_plate1.csv")

# Parameters (adjust per run)
rxn_vol       <- 20     # µL total ddPCR reaction volume
input_vol     <- 5      # µL extract added to reaction
elution_vol   <- 100    # µL total DNA extract
dilution      <- 10     # dilution factor applied to extract before reaction

# Dry soil mass (g) per sample -- join from sample metadata
metadata <- read_csv("sample_metadata.csv")  # cols: Sample, dry_soil_g

results <- raw |>
  filter(AcceptedDroplets >= 10000) |>      # droplet count filter
  left_join(metadata, by = "Sample") |>
  mutate(
    copies_per_g = Concentration *           # copies/µL in reaction
      rxn_vol *                              # total reaction volume
      dilution *                             # dilution correction
      (elution_vol / input_vol) *            # extraction recovery
      (1 / dry_soil_g)                       # normalize to dry soil
  )

# Flag QC issues
results <- results |>
  mutate(
    qc_flag = case_when(
      AcceptedDroplets < 10000              ~ "low_droplets",
      Concentration == 0 & !is.na(copies_per_g) ~ "no_signal",
      TRUE                                  ~ "OK"
    )
  )

write_csv(results, "2025-05-14_amoA_wetland_plate1_processed.csv")
```


## Interpreting Relative Gene Abundances

Individual gene copy numbers are most informative when examined in
relation to each other and to the soil's total microbial biomass (often
estimated as 16S rRNA gene copies) [@levybooth2014; @kuypers2018].

Suggested derived metrics:

| Metric | Formula | Ecological interpretation |
|:-------|:--------|:--------------------------|
| AOB : AOA ratio | *amoA*(AOB) / *amoA*(AOA) | Relative dominance of bacterial vs. archaeal nitrifiers |
| Denitrification potential | *nirK* + *nirS* + *nosZ* | Combined capacity for N loss as gas |
| N~2~O consumer : producer | *nosZ* / (*nirK* + *nirS*) | Capacity to complete denitrification; low values predict N~2~O accumulation |
| Diazotroph index | *nifH* / 16S | Fraction of community with N fixation capacity |
| DNRA : denitrification | *nrfA* / (*nirK* + *nirS*) | N retention vs. N loss balance |

## Training Record

Before performing ddPCR data analysis independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L701](SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd)
   in full
2. Review the DMINQ reporting standard [@dmiqe2020]
3. Demonstrate correct QuantaSoft threshold setting on at least two
   plates under supervision
4. Run the copy number normalization R script on a test dataset and
   reproduce the trainer's results
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: DMINQ Checklist {.appendix}

When reporting ddPCR data from this workflow, include the following
metadata per @dmiqe2020:

| Item                          | Required by DMINQ | Notes |
|:------------------------------|:------------------|:------|
| Instrument model and serial   | Yes | Bio-Rad QX200 |
| Software version              | Yes | QuantaSoft version |
| Droplet count per well        | Yes | Must be ≥ 10,000 |
| Threshold setting method      | Yes | Manual or automated; document both |
| NTC result                    | Yes | Copies/µL; must be 0 or < 3 positive droplets |
| Positive control              | Yes | gBlock; expected and measured concentration |
| Rain percentage               | Yes | Document even if low |
| Dilution factor               | Yes |   |
| Normalization denominator     | Yes | Dry soil mass (g) and/or DNA (ng) |
| Inhibition check result       | Yes | 1:5 vs. 1:10 dilution agreement |
| Primer/probe sequences        | Yes | Or cite SOP-L701 registry |
| Cycling conditions            | Yes | Annealing temperature, cycles |
| Reference for target gene     | Yes | Cite from SOP-L701 registry |
